items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Guy Béart introduced him to the audience... We played two numbers for Duke... Later, he played two numbers with us

ctx.x: We were all very excited to be with Duke. He came on the T.V. set at 5 p.m., dressed in a light blue costume(it was in July). Guy Béart introduced him to the audience, because Guy Béart always had his emission semi-public with personalities, artists, guests, press, and a lot of beautiful girls, who were engaged especially to add more class to the show.

We played twonnumbers for Duke, than Béart asked him a lot of questions about his career, about jazz.."what is jazz? what is the future of jazz?....what do you think of free jazz?...do you sing?... please sing a song...." Duke has a superb sense of humour, and he knows how to wrangle his way out of the most tricky situation...it was a pleasure to hear him talk.

Then he sat at the piano and played some of his compositions. Later,he played two numbers with us, and at the end, we had a jam session. Nothing had been prepared or rehearsed in advance. The atmosphere was terrific. I was amazed at the patience of Duke. It was 1 a.m. when shw show was finished. For unknown reasons, it was two years before the programme was shown on T.V.
